data.taskBrief:
TASK BRIEF: Update an existing YouTube video and return the updated video resource (YouTube Data API v3)

FIT
Partially. This request can update an existing video’s metadata and visibility, and it uses OAuth permissions, but the supplied schema only shows one `snippet.localized` object rather than six localized titles/descriptions. It also warns that `part` controls which mutable fields are overwritten, so “preserve existing metadata” is only possible for fields not included in the update parts.

AUTH
OAuth 2.0 Bearer token
Header: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` or access token via the `access_token` query parameter; this request’s collection auth says the token is added to the header.
Required permissions from the collection: YouTube scopes such as `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube`, `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.force-ssl`, or `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.upload` may apply depending on the video update being performed.

BASE URL
https://youtube.googleapis.com

STEPS
1. PUT /youtube/v3/videos
   Params:
   - `part` (query, array, required): selects which resource parts are updated and which parts are returned. Example: `snippet,status`.
   - `onBehalfOfContentOwner` (query, string, optional): content-owner identifier for YouTube content partners. Example: `on-behalf-of-content-owner-here`.
   - `Authorization` (header, Bearer token): OAuth 2.0 access token from the collection auth.
   - JSON body fields used by this schema include `id` (string, video ID), `snippet.title` (string), `snippet.defaultLanguage` (string), `snippet.defaultAudioLanguage` (string), `snippet.description` (string), `snippet.channelId` (string), `snippet.channelTitle` (string), `snippet.categoryId` (string), `snippet.publishedAt` (string date-time), `snippet.liveBroadcastContent` (string), `snippet.tags` (array of strings), and `status.privacyStatus` (string such as `public`). The body schema also includes many additional optional resource fields; only the fields present in the request body are shown here.
   Returns: 200 with the updated video resource. The example response includes `id`, `snippet.title`, `snippet.defaultLanguage`, `snippet.description`, `status.privacyStatus`, `status.uploadStatus`, `status.license`, `contentDetails.definition`, `processingDetails.processingStatus`, `statistics.viewCount`, `player.embedHtml`, and `etag` among many other fields.
   Threading: None

GOTCHAS
- `part` is required and controls both what gets updated and what comes back in the response.
- This endpoint can overwrite mutable fields in the parts named in `part`; it is not a blanket “preserve everything” patch.
- The supplied body schema shows a single `snippet.localized` object, not six separate localizations.
- `status.privacyStatus` is in the body and is the field shown for setting public visibility.
- The request body is JSON and the headers include `Content-Type: application/json`.
- If `onBehalfOfContentOwner` is used, it is only for YouTube content partners.
